name: Score new trial signups against your ICP with one AI agent and looot and alert Slack on hot leads

parameters.content:
## Score every new trial signup and post the hot ones to Slack

### How it works
1. Your app posts each new signup to the webhook: `{"email": "...", "name": "..."}`.
2. Free mail addresses stop at **Free mail, skipped** and cost nothing.
3. For work emails, one AI agent looks up the person and the company through looot and reads the company homepage, then scores the fit from 0 to 100 against your ICP.
4. Hot signups (70 or more) go to Slack with title, company, size and the reason. Edit the ICP line in the system message.

One looot credential replaces the Firecrawl and Scrapin.io accounts this flow usually needs.

**Cost per signup**, from looot's public catalog on 2026-10-31: person from email from $0.0036, company data $0.0019, page read from $0.0002. About $0.006 per work email signup. Each call is capped at $0.03 and the agent at 6 steps, so a signup can never cost more than $0.18. Model tokens are billed by OpenAI.

### Setup
- Needs the verified community node **n8n-nodes-looot** (built against 0.1.4): Settings > Community nodes > Install, search `looot`. [Install guide](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/verified-install/)
- looot: sign up at [looot.ai](https://looot.ai), top up (from $5), create an agent token under Settings > Agent tokens, then add a **looot API** credential in n8n.
- OpenAI and Slack credentials. Set the channel ID in **Post to Slack**.
- Point your signup event at the production webhook URL.
- Self-hosted n8n: set `N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_ALLOW_TOOL_USAGE=true` so the agent can use the looot node as a tool.

### Customization
Change HOT and WARM in **Score and route**. Add a HubSpot or Instantly node on the hot branch.

options.systemMessage:
You score new trial signups for a sales team.
ICP: B2B software companies with 20 to 2,000 employees; buyers in sales, marketing, RevOps or the founding team. Edit this line for your buyer.
1. job:people.enrich.by-email with {"email": "..."} for name, title and LinkedIn.
2. job:company.enrich with {"domain": "..."} for size, industry and country.
3. job:web.scrape.markdown on https://<domain> to see what the company sells.
fit_score 0 to 100. reason: one sentence with the facts behind the score. Never invent data.

parameters.toolDescription:
Runs one looot data call and returns the run: status, result and actualCost. Every call is capped. Use only these ids and inputs:
- job:people.enrich.by-email, input {"email": "ada@example.com"}: the person behind an email.
- job:company.enrich, input {"domain": "example.com"}: company size, industry, country.
- job:web.scrape.markdown, input {"url": "https://example.com"}: one page as text.
parameters.endpointId: ={{ $fromAI('endpointId', 'A looot job or endpoint id from the tool description', 'string') }}
parameters.input: ={{ $fromAI('input', 'The input object, with the field names the tool description gives for that id', 'json') }}
parameters.idempotencyKey: ={{ ('n8n-' + $execution.id + '-' + $fromAI('endpointId', 'A looot job or endpoint id from the tool description', 'string') + '-' + JSON.stringify($fromAI('input', 'The input object, with the field names the tool description gives for that id', 'json'))).slice(0, 200) }}
